title: Store materials on a floor under construction
instruction: This is one bay of a floor in a building under construction, at 1:50 scale. Store the three bundles of material in this bay where US federal construction rules allow.
context: Material stored near a hoistway or a building's open edge can fall onto workers below. 29 CFR 1926.250(b)(1): "Material stored inside buildings under construction shall not be placed within 6 feet of any hoistway or inside floor openings, nor within 10 feet of an exterior wall which does not extend above the top of the material stored." A full-height wall doesn't limit storage; a parapet lower than the material does. Done by: construction laborers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. A grey concrete floor slab, fixed and 4 mm thick, runs from 8 to 40 cm out from the bases and 45 cm to each side of the midline. Storage is on this slab only. A 50 mm square hoistway (the shaft of a material hoist) is cut through it, 21.5 to 26.5 cm out and 9.5 to 14.5 cm left of the midline; its bottom is a black plate 3 mm below the slab. The slab's far edge is the building's outside edge: a fixed concrete wall 12 mm thick and 61 mm tall above the slab runs along it right of the midline, and a fixed concrete parapet 12 mm thick and 12 mm tall runs along it left of the midline. Three bundles of building material, each a 24 x 30 x 18 mm block of 60 g (tan lumber, white drywall, pink insulation), lie on the slab with their 30 mm side left to right: lumber centred 24 cm out and 7 cm left, 10 mm from the hoistway's right edge; insulation 29.2 cm out and 12 cm left, 15 mm beyond the hoistway; drywall 38 cm out and 20 cm left, 8 mm from the parapet.
scoring: Distances are at scale (1 ft = 6.1 mm), from a bundle's outline seen from above. A bundle is stored when it lies on any face (within 10 degrees of flat) on the slab or on another bundle (bottom within 2 mm), its centre over the slab and inside the outside walls; at least 6 ft (36.6 mm) from the hoistway's edge; and at least 10 ft (61 mm) from each outside wall whose top is no higher than the top of the material stored with it (the highest top among the bundles stacked or touching with it). The parapet is lower than any bundle; the full wall counts only for a stack that reaches its top. A third for each stored bundle; 1.0 when all three are stored and still for 1 s, which ends the trial. A bundle in the hoistway, off the slab or held in the air scores nothing.
reset_notes: Put the bundles back beside the hoistway and the parapet as in the setup.
fidelity: The building is at 1:50; the bundles are about 1.2 x 1.5 x 0.9 m at that scale, solid blocks rather than strapped stacks of boards or sheets. The hoistway is a 3 mm recess, not a hole through the floor. The slab and walls are fixed. Every object, the slab and walls included, has rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); only the table under the slab uses the sim's default (0.5).
